questions.prompt: Prove that m∠A + m∠B + m∠C = 180° in triangle ABC. Draw the line through C parallel to AB.
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that m∠A + m∠B + m∠C = 180° in triangle ABC. Draw the line through C parallel to AB.
questions.required_method: Name the two new angles at C, use alternate interior angles with AB, and the straight angle at C.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: (1) through C there is exactly one line parallel to AB (parallel postulate); (2) the angles it makes with CA and CB are congruent to ∠A and ∠B (alternate interior angles, transversals CA and CB); (3) those two angles and ∠ACB form a straight angle, 180°; (4) substitute. Invalid: measuring angles; citing the exterior angle theorem, because in this course that theorem is proved FROM the angle sum (set 20, FORWARD 1), so using it here would be circular.

questions.required_method: Use the straight angle ABD at B, the translation (∠C′BD ≅ ∠A), and alternate interior angles (BC′ ∥ AC).
